title: Brazil’s Sovereignty Is on the Ballot
gist: Main and Long argue a Flavio Bolsonaro win in Brazil's Oct. 25 runoff would open the door to US military activity via terrorism designations of Brazilian gangs and the Shield of the Americas, with Ecuador as preview, and tie it to critical-mineral access.

insights.claim: Prediction markets favored Flavio Bolsonaro in the runoff even though a May scandal over a request for about $27 million from a jailed banker had sunk his polls.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: Market odds favor a Bolsonaro win, relevant to Brazilian assets.

insights.claim: Trump received Flavio on May 26 and Rubio designated Brazil's biggest gangs as foreign terrorist organizations two days later, shifting the campaign from corruption to insecurity.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: US designations are an electoral lever; they also bring military options.

insights.claim: The FTO designations follow tariffs on Brazilian exports and sanctions on the justice who prosecuted Jair Bolsonaro, and resemble US efforts in elections in Argentina, Colombia and Honduras.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: Trade and sanction risk toward Brazil depends on the election result.

insights.claim: Treating cartels as FTOs underpinned Operation Southern Spear boat strikes killing 239 people, which the authors say did not curb fentanyl, which comes overland from Mexico.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: The doctrine converts law enforcement into military action across the hemisphere.

insights.claim: The Jan. 3 US attack on Venezuela and abduction of Maduro killed an estimated 75 and was linked to an FTO designation.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: Shows designation can precede force against a state.

insights.claim: Shield of the Americas members endorsed a declaration calling for invoking the 1947 Rio Treaty against nonstate criminal groups; Flavio reportedly promised Brazil would join.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: A Bolsonaro win could bring Brazil into a US-led security bloc.

insights.claim: In Ecuador under Noboa, US forces operate from Manta and Taura despite a constitutional ban on foreign bases, and the air force commander who asked for operational control was removed within two days.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: Shows the sovereignty cost of tight US security ties.

insights.claim: Flavio pitches Brazil as the answer to US dependence on China for rare earths with a strategic minerals partnership, while Lula favors multilateralism and strategic autonomy.
insights.speaker: Alexander Main, Guillaume Long
insights.so_what: A Bolsonaro win would favor US-Brazil minerals deals; Lula keeps balancing.
